subject: Money
title: The Great Depression
description: A 60-second lesson on The Great Depression.

hook.text: Between 1929 and 1933, U.S. prices fell 25%. A quarter of workers were unemployed. Banks vanished overnight.

buildup.text: The stock crash triggered bank runs. Banks collapsed, money supply shrank, and spending froze.

discovery.text: Deflation made the depression worse. With falling prices, businesses cut wages, workers cut spending, demand collapsed.

twist.text: The Fed did nothing—it let banks fail. Modern economists agree that passivity turned a recession into a catastrophe.

climax.text: The lesson: in deflation, governments must act fast and aggressively. Delay is the deadliest policy.

punchline.text: Doing nothing was the worst thing to do.

quiz.question: How did the Fed's response make the Great Depression worse?
options: It raised interest rates too high
It let banks fail without intervention
